descriptors.definition: Model tax conventions serve as standardized frameworks developed by international bodies like the OECD and UN to assist nations in bilateral tax treaty negotiations. While non-binding by themselves, these models provide foundational principles, with the OECD model prioritizing residence-based taxation and the UN model balancing source-based and residence-based taxation.
inclusion: Reference points for bilateral tax negotiations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between the OECD model favoring residence taxation and the UN model prioritizing source-based taxation.

descriptors.concept_name: Title and Preamble Framework of Model Conventions
descriptors.definition: The titles and preambles of the OECD and UN model conventions establish the mutual intent of contracting states to eliminate double taxation while preventing tax avoidance, evasion, and abusive treaty-shopping arrangements. Both models contain nearly identical language addressing economic cooperation and the restriction of unintentional non-taxation or reduced taxation benefits.
inclusion: UN Model Convention title and preamble text
OECD Model Convention title and preamble comparison
exclusion: Substantive distributive rules of specific articles
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general treaty objectives stated in the preamble and operational distributive rules found in subsequent articles.
